record.original_question: For a continuous function f on T^1(X) with the stated cusp growth condition, badly approximable α∈R, and 0<c1<c2, do the averages M^{-1}∑_{m=1}^M f(u_y(αm)) converge uniformly to the Liouville integral as M→∞ for c1M^{-2}≤y≤c2M^{-2}?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 22 (J. Marklof, A. Strömbergsson) . Let f be a continuous function on T 1(X ) with given growth condition at the cusps (see [182]). Then for α ∈ R which is badly approximable by rationals and 0 < c1 < c2, 1 M M∑ m= 1 f (uy (αm)) → ∫ T1(X ) f d λ uniformly as M → ∞ and c1M − 2 ≤ y ≤ c2M − 2, where λ denotes the Liouville mea-sure.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H} = \{z = x+iy : y>0\}$ denote the upper half-plane with hyperbolic metric, on which $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ acts by Möbius transformations. Let $\Gamma = \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$, let $X = \Gamma\backslash\mathbb{H}$ be the modular surface, and let $T^1(X)$ be its unit tangent bundle, identified with $\Gamma\backslash\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. Let $\lambda$ denote the Liouville (Haar) probability measure on $T^1(X)$. For $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and $y>0$, define the horocycle element
$$u_y(t) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & t \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} y^{1/2} & 0 \\ 0 & y^{-1/2} \end{pmatrix},$$
viewed as a point in $T^1(X)$ via the projection $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R}) \to \Gamma\backslash\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. A real number $\alpha$ is called badly approximable by rationals if there exists $c>0$ such that $|\alpha - p/q| \geq c/q^2$ for every $p/q \in \mathbb{Q}$. Fix constants $0 < c_1 < c_2$. Consider continuous functions $f : T^1(X) \to \mathbb{C}$ that satisfy a prescribed growth condition at the cusp ensuring all averages below are well defined (e.g., $|f(g)| \ll y(g)^{1-\delta}$ for some $\delta>0$, where $y(g)$ is the imaginary part of the base point of $g$).

Prove or disprove: for every such $f$ and every badly approximable $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$,
$$\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^M f\bigl(u_y(\alpha m)\bigr) \;\longrightarrow\; \int_{T^1(X)} f\, d\lambda$$
as $M \to \infty$, uniformly in $y$ with $c_1 M^{-2} \leq y \leq c_2 M^{-2}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open conjecture attributed to Marklof and Strömbergsson. Related results are known: Marklof–Strömbergsson (GAFA 2003) proved equidistribution of Kronecker sequences along closed horocycles for almost every α and y ≫ N^{-δ}, and subsequent works treat various scaling regimes, but the cusp-scale regime y ≍ M^{-2} for badly approximable α does not appear to be resolved. No reference confirming a complete proof was found.

status_evidence.title: Equidistribution of Kronecker sequences along closed horocycles
status_evidence.snippet: Equidistribution for almost every α with y > N^{-δ}, in the metaplectic cover of SL(2,R).
status_evidence.claim: Establishes related equidistribution at scales above the cusp-scale; does not resolve the badly-approximable case at y ≍ M^{-2}.

status_evidence.title: Shrinking target equidistribution of horocycles in cusps
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on horocycle equidistribution in cusps.
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates the cusp-scale regime is an active research area without resolving the stated conjecture.
